chunks: By Allāh, I have been taught the conveyance of messages, the fulfilment of waiting periods, and the completion of words.
And with us—the People of the House—are the doors of wisdom and the light of authority.
Beware, the laws of religion are one, and its paths are straight. He who adheres to them attains and succeeds, and he who refrains from them goes astray and regrets.

key_terms.أَبْوَابُ الْحُكْمِ: Doors of wisdom/judgment, indicating deep knowledge and authority
key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt), referring to the Prophet's family and Imams

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Ahl al-Bayt's role in understanding Islamic laws according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes the Ahl al-Bayt as the custodians of divine authority (*Abwab al-Hukm*) and the interpreters of Sharia, emphasizing that their guidance is the singular, straight path to salvation. This assertion underscores the Shia doctrine of the infallible Imams' role in preserving and elucidating the complete message of Islam, warning that deviation from this divinely appointed path results in spiritual loss.

en.sayed-ali-raza: By Allāh, I have knowledge of the conveyance of messages, fulfilment of promises and of entire expressions.
We the people of the house (of the Prophet — Ahlu’l-bayt) possess the doors of wisdom and light of governance.

Beware that the paths of religion are one and its highways are straight. He who follows them achieves (the aim) and secures (the objective). And he who stood away from it went astray and incurred repentance.
